title: Why I'm Buying These 3 Stocks (Ignore the AI Hype)
creator: Asymmetric Investing
summary: Travis Hoium pitches his three cheapest current holdings - all trading at single-digit forward multiples he expects to re-rate as growth and margins compound - and says he has been accumulating all three through 2026, rebutting the market's two core fears (autonomous vehicles killing ride-hail, gaming demand peaking). Lyft (LYFT) - BUY: >30M active riders, ~1B rides a year, $1.1B TTM free cash flow, net-cash balance sheet; ~8x forward P/E, ~5x forward P/FCF; the AV-disruption fear is overblown given the Waymo partnership, the European taxi foothold and potential acquirer appeal at this multiple (he would not be surprised if "a Waymo buys them, a Zoox buys them"); his stated bear case is Lyft falling to #4 in autonomy if Tesla and Waymo enter. Uber (UBER) - BUY: gross bookings, trips, monthly riders (28M) and delivery all compounding; mobility CAGR 22%, delivery ~19%; his bull case is Uber as the demand-aggregator for every AV player a decade out. MGM Resorts (MGM) - BUY: EV/EBITDA and P/FCF both below 8x on a $7.5B market cap with ~$1B/year buybacks (~15% of shares); the real catalyst is 2030 MGM Japan in Osaka (~$10B property), where a Marina Bay Sands proxy (~$6B revenue, ~$3B adjusted EBITDA) implies MGM's 44% stake alone could be worth the whole market cap. TSLA appears only as an AV competitive risk (his standing Sep 30 SELL unchanged); IAC (Barry Diller's company, failed MGM buyout), Entain, LVS and Lucid are passing mentions with no calls. Caption garbles: "Whimo"/"Zuks" for Waymo/Zoox, "People, Inc." for IAC, "Antain" for Entain; no price targets were garbled because none were given.
